steps.body: A parabola has a remarkable property: **every ray coming straight in, parallel to the axis, reflects to the focus** — and rays from the focus reflect out parallel. This is why satellite dishes, headlights, and solar cookers are parabolic: they concentrate incoming signal at the focus, or beam a source outward.

widget.prompt: A satellite dish is a parabola. Where should the receiver be placed to catch all incoming parallel signals?

options.label: At the focus
options.feedback: Right — parallel rays all reflect to the focus, so that's where the signal concentrates.

options.label: At the vertex
options.feedback: The vertex is the curve's tip; the rays converge at the FOCUS, not the vertex.

options.label: On the directrix
options.feedback: The directrix is a construction line, not on the dish. Rays converge at the focus.

steps.body: The focal length p sets how deep the dish is. A small p gives a deep, tightly-curved dish with the focus close to the vertex; a large p gives a shallow dish with a distant focus. Designers choose p to place the receiver conveniently while capturing the beam.

explanationVariants: For a dish y = x²/(4p) with p = 2, the receiver (focus) sits p = 2 units above the vertex.
The focus is always p above the vertex: here 2 units.

widget.prompt: A parabolic dish is y = x²/8. How far above the vertex should the receiver sit? (That's p.)

commonErrors.feedback: p = 8/4 = 2, so the receiver is 2 units above the vertex.

explanationVariants: A flashlight puts its bulb at the focus so the reflected rays leave parallel — a tight, straight beam.
Source at the focus → parallel outgoing rays, the reverse of the dish.

widget.prompt: In a flashlight with a parabolic mirror, placing the bulb at the focus produces:

options.label: A parallel beam of light
options.feedback: Right — rays from the focus reflect outward parallel to the axis.

options.label: A spread-out, scattered glow
options.feedback: The focus placement does the opposite: it makes a tight PARALLEL beam.

options.label: Light that converges to a point
options.feedback: Convergence happens for INCOMING parallel rays. A source AT the focus beams out parallel.

steps.body: Work forward: from focus to width.
explanationVariants: A dish with p = 3 is shaped x² = 4(3)y = 12y. At height y = 3, x² = 12(3) = 36, so x = 6 — and since the dish is symmetric, its full tip-to-tip width there is 2(6) = 12.
Plug y = 3 into x² = 12y: x² = 36, x = 6, so the width is 2 × 6 = 12.

widget.prompt: A parabolic dish has its focus (receiver) p = 3 units above the vertex, so x² = 4py = 12y. How WIDE is the dish, tip to tip, at a height of 3 units above the vertex?

commonErrors.feedback: 6 = x is the distance from the center line to one edge. The WIDTH is tip-to-tip: 2 × 6 = 12.
36 = x², before the square root. Take the root first (x = 6), then double it for the width: 12.

widget.fallbackFeedback: x² = 12(3) = 36 → x = 6; the width tip-to-tip is 2 × 6 = 12.

explanationVariants: x² = 20y means 4p = 20, p = 5 — a shallow dish with the focus 5 units out.

widget.prompt: A dish is designed as x² = 20y. How far from the vertex is the focus?

commonErrors.feedback: Halving gives 10, but the form is x² = 4py, so 20 = 4p — not 2p. That makes p = 5.

steps.body: Geometry you can point at the sky.
takeaways: Parallel rays reflect to the focus; focus-sourced rays leave parallel.
Dishes, headlights, and solar cookers all exploit this.
Focal length p tunes the dish's depth and focus distance.

concept.body: Parabolic reflectors send parallel incoming rays to the focus (and focus-sourced rays out parallel). The receiver/source belongs at the focus, p units from the vertex.

explanationVariants: Incoming parallel signals converge at the focus — put the receiver there.
The focus is the collection point.

widget.prompt: Incoming parallel radio waves on a parabolic dish converge at the:

options.label: Focus
options.feedback: Right — that's the parabola's reflective property.

options.label: Vertex
options.feedback: They converge at the FOCUS, not the vertex.

options.label: Edge
options.feedback: The convergence point is the focus.
